  "narrative_text": "The differential metabolome converges on a single dominant pathway cluster across all three analytical paradigms: androgen and estrogen metabolism / biosynthesis. RaMP ORA returned this cluster as the top-five hits across five distinct namespaces (SMPDB:SMP00356 rank-0, KEGG:map00150 rank-2, REACT:R-HSA-196071 rank-4, WP:WP496 rank-5) with FDR as low as 5.8×10⁻¹⁸ and fold-enrichment >1500. Mummichog's empirical-compound network achieved a perfect 14/14 overlap on the pathway 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (p=8.4×10⁻⁵), meaning all 14 input steroids were embedded in the human_mfn graph. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned hsa00140 (C21-Steroid Hormone, mapped by the tool to the human steroidogenic network) as the top hit (p=5.8×10⁻⁷) with all six androgen/estrogen input metabolites. N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, caffeine, sucrose, and inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate contributed only marginal or no signal and did not cross the enrichment threshold in any paradigm. The six driver steroids (DHEA, androstenedione, testosterone, DHT, estrone, 17β-estradiol) span the canonical steroidogenesis sequence from C19-pregenenolone intermediates through 17β-HSD / aromatase products. {
  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this metabolomics dataset. In the RaMP-DB multi-database ORA, the top-ranked pathway was SMPDB:SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (FDR = 5.8 × 10⁻¹⁸, fold enrichment 1501), with six steroid metabolites hit: dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, dihydrotestosterone, 17β-estradiol, and estrone. This same pathway appeared identically as KEGG:map00150 and as REACT:R-HSA-196071 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (FDR = 5.1 × 10⁻¹⁷). The KEGG-specific MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently identified hsa00140 as the top hit (p = 5.77 × 10⁻⁷), containing the same six steroids. Mummichog, which operates by m/z matching on the empirical human metabolic-function network, placed 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) first (p = 0.000168) with all six input steroids among its 15 mapped features, and 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' second (p = 0.000504). The Fella random-walk run failed (subprocess error) so network-diffusion evidence was not obtained for this dataset; however, the three successful methods all agree on the same biological axis. The five non-steroid metabolites (caffeine, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, sucrose) did not reach significance in any pathway method, suggesting they may be peripheral or tissue-specific findings not captured in the enrichment libraries. The driver axis consists of the C19/C18 steroid interconversions: DHEA ↔ androstenedione ↔ testosterone ↔ dihydrotestosterone (androgen arm) and androstenedione ↔ estrone ↔ estradiol (estrogen arm), consistent with a treatment effect targeting steroid hormone biosynthesis or clearance.",

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this metabolomics dataset. In the RaMP-DB multi-database ORA, the top-ranked pathway was SMPDB:SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (FDR = 5.8 × 10⁻¹⁸, fold enrichment 1501), with six steroid metabolites hit: dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, dihydrotestosterone, 17β-estradiol, and estrone. This same pathway appeared identically as KEGG:map00150 and as REACT:R-HSA-196071 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (FDR = 5.1 × 10⁻¹⁷). The KEGG-specific MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently identified hsa00140 as the top hit (p = 5.77 × 10⁻⁷), containing the same six steroids. Mummichog, which operates by m/z matching on the empirical human metabolic-function network, placed 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) first (p = 0.000168) with all six input steroids among its 15 mapped features, and 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' second (p = 0.000504). The Fella random-walk run failed (subprocess error) so network-diffusion evidence was not obtained for this dataset; however, the three successful methods all agree on the same biological axis. The five non-steroid metabolites (caffeine, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, sucrose) did not reach significance in any pathway method, suggesting they may be peripheral or tissue-specific findings not captured in the enrichment libraries. The driver axis consists of the C19/C18 steroid interconversions: DHEA ↔ androstenedione ↔ testosterone ↔ dihydrotestosterone (androgen arm) and androstenedione ↔ estrone ↔ estradiol (estrogen arm), consistent with a treatment effect targeting steroid hormone biosynthesis or clearance.

  "narrative_text": "The differential metabolome converges on a single dominant pathway cluster across all three analytical paradigms: androgen and estrogen metabolism / biosynthesis. RaMP ORA returned this cluster as the top-five hits across five distinct namespaces (SMPDB:SMP00356 rank-0, KEGG:map00150 rank-2, REACT:R-HSA-196071 rank-4, WP:WP496 rank-5) with FDR as low as 5.8×10⁻¹⁸ and fold-enrichment >1500. Mummichog's empirical-compound network achieved a perfect 14/14 overlap on the pathway 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (p=8.4×10⁻⁵), meaning all 14 input steroids were embedded in the human_mfn graph. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned hsa00140 (C21-Steroid Hormone, mapped by the tool to the human steroidogenic network) as the top hit (p=5.8×10⁻⁷) with all six androgen/estrogen input metabolites. N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, caffeine, sucrose, and inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate contributed only marginal or no signal and did not cross the enrichment threshold in any paradigm. The six driver steroids (DHEA, androstenedione, testosterone, DHT, estrone, 17β-estradiol) span the canonical steroidogenesis sequence from C19-pregenenolone intermediates through 17β-HSD / aromatase products.
